title: The Slav Defence
standfirst: If the Queen's Gambit Declined bothers you because of that bishop on c8, the Slav is the answer — and the parallel with the Caro-Kann is exact.

steps.title: The same fix, a different opening
body: In the Queen's Gambit Declined, Black supports d5 with …e6 and shuts in the light-squared bishop. The Slav supports it with the c-pawn instead.
If that sounds familiar, it should — it's precisely what the Caro-Kann does against 1.e4. The same idea travels.

steps.title: The offer
body: White attacks d5 from the side.

steps.title: Support d5, keep the bishop free
body: The defining move. It does the same job as …e6 in the QGD — hold d5 with a pawn — but leaves the c8–h3 diagonal open for the bishop.

steps.title: Natural development
body: White develops and stops …e5 in one move.

steps.title: Guard the centre
body: Black's most natural developing move, adding a defender to d5.

steps.title: Pile on d5
body: Both sides continue to argue about the same square.

steps.title: Now taking actually works
body: In the QGD, grabbing this pawn is bad because White regains it with a big centre. Here it's the main line — because Black has …b5 available to hold the pawn, thanks to the c6 pawn supporting it.
The same little pawn move that freed the bishop also makes the capture playable. One move, two jobs.

steps.title: Stop the pawn being held
body: White's answer: take b5 away before it happens. He'll regain the c4 pawn next.
The cost is that a4 permanently weakens b4 — a square Black's pieces will use later. Almost every move in a good opening is a trade like this.

steps.title: Out, before anything blocks it
body: There's the bishop, on the diagonal the QGD never gives it. This is what the whole system was for.

steps.title: Solid, and now harmless
body: White shuts in his own dark-squared bishop, but as in the QGD it will find a path. Both sides are simply completing development.

steps.title: Now the pawn goes there, second
body: The exact Caro-Kann trick: the pawn only comes to e6 after the bishop has left. Compare this position to the Queen's Gambit Declined — same structure, better bishop.
White will play Bxc4 and castle with a small space advantage. Black is solid, has no bad pieces, and knows exactly what he's playing for.
